plan.title: [framework-gap] Keep orientation state local and separate freshness domains

narratives.Description: [framework-gap] Keep orientation state local and separate freshness domains
narratives.Overview:
## Status and scope

Confirmed against v0.108.0 and current `master`.

This issue owns orientation-state tracking hygiene and explicit freshness-domain wording. It does not redesign the full occupancy/ritual/session-bind protocol.

## Summary

Keep `.deft/orientation-state.json` local so routine session orientation cannot dirty a clean consumer checkout, and state explicitly that orientation/session-bind freshness is not lifecycle authority.

## Confirmed implementation evidence

- Orientation state is a deposit/tooling fast-path record containing timestamps and command outcomes: [`orientation-state.ts:12-30`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/orientation-state.ts#L12-L30).
- Orientation persists that record by default: [`orientation-compression.ts:532-561`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/session/orientation-compression.ts#L532-L561).
- The canonical consumer ignore baseline omits `.deft/orientation-state.json`: [`gitignore.ts:34-53`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts#L34-L53).
- Existing tests assert persistence but do not assert clean-tree behavior.

The filing audit found the artifact tracked or dirty in multiple existing worktrees. Those counts are environment-specific context; the deterministic defect is the writer plus the missing canonical ignore/migration rule.

## Freshness boundary already established

The v0.108.0 freshness contract defines session-bind generation over loaded deposit surfaces such as payload, version, templates, skills, and docs. It does not establish branch, ordered-plan, scope, or lifecycle authority: [`freshness-contract.md:8-30`](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/v0.108.0/content/docs/freshness-contract.md#L8-L30).

This issue should make that non-authority boundary explicit, not add lifecycle generations to session-bind as an incidental fix.

## Reproduction

1. Start from a clean consumer checkout where `.deft/orientation-state.json` is trackable or already tracked.
2. Run an orientation path that refreshes timestamps or surface results.
3. Run `git status --short`.
4. Observe a product-unrelated change to orientation state.

## Expected behavior

Orientation fast-path state is local runtime/cache state. Init and update should ignore it selectively and migrate existing consumers without deleting the user's local data. Cold start, re-arm, doctor, agents refresh, and cache-fresh orientation paths should leave a clean checkout clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Classify every orientation-state field as local cache/runtime state.
- [ ] Add `.deft/orientation-state.json` to every canonical consumer ignore generator/source.
- [ ] Heal existing consumer `.gitignore` files idempotently during the supported update/migration path.
- [ ] Stop tracking an existing orientation artifact without deleting the local file unexpectedly.
- [ ] Document orientation state and session-bind as deposit/toolchain freshness only, not branch/plan/scope/lifecycle authority.
- [ ] Add clean-tree regression coverage for cold start, re-arm, doctor, agents refresh, and cache-fresh orientation paths.
- [ ] Verify repeated orientation remains a functional fast path after the tracking migration.

## Out of scope

- Acquire-before-mutate session ordering (#3906).
- Repository-wide lifecycle authority (#3910).
- A full redesign of ritual, bind, occupancy, release, expiry, and crash postconditions (track under #3613 or a bounded child).

## Related

- #3612 — other unignored `.deft` runtime artifacts
- #3613 — occupancy-model tracker
- #3906 — acquire occupancy before startup mutations
- #1618 — source-of-truth versus materialized views
